title: Report cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours
summary: Under CERT-In's Directions of 28 April 2022, specified cyber incidents must be reported within 6 hours of noticing them. ICT system logs must be kept for 180 days within India, and system clocks synchronised to NIC or NPL time servers.
action: Keep an incident-reporting contact and runbook ready, and check that log retention meets 180 days.

title: Use NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 as your checklist
summary: CSF 2.0, released in February 2024, adds a sixth function, Govern, to Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover. It applies to organisations of any size.
action: Map your current controls to the six functions and fix the biggest gaps first.

title: Start planning for post-quantum cryptography
summary: NIST published its first post-quantum standards in August 2024: FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA).
action: List where you use RSA and ECC, and prioritise systems that protect long-lived data.

title: Use phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication
summary: NIST digital identity guidelines recommend multi-factor authentication, and phishing-resistant methods for higher-risk access.
action: Turn on MFA for all admin, remote and email access, starting with privileged accounts.
